clue.text: Success — clear tape patched up historic Russian building

parts.note: a success is a win

indicators.note: something patched up has been mended and put back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restoration job on a famous Russian landmark, with clear sticky tape doing the repairs successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patched up' signals the anagram; 'tape' tempts as a repair material but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter Palace in St Petersburg was the official residence of the Russian tsars, stormed in 1917.

clue.text: Unusual deviation on the rise, getting banned

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so from bottom to top

parts.note: yaw is a deviation from a course, as of a ship or aircraft
something banned is out, no longer allowed

explanation.surface: Some deviant behaviour is on the increase and is being banned as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns YAW upwards into WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Way-out is informal for strikingly unconventional or eccentric, a synonym of unusual.

clue.text: Einstein's decade?

parts.note: the question mark flags a playful definition: a whimsical label for a decade linked to a famous genius, which turns out to be the nickname of a historical era

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking which decade the great physicist belonged to.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful link is that Einstein was a boy in the 1890s, the decade nicknamed for its loose Victorian morals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Naughty Nineties is the popular nickname for the 1890s, when Albert Einstein was a teenager.

clue.text: Arab leader always imprisoning me

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding the following word inside a cell, so it goes within the first

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A complaint that a desert ruler keeps locking the speaker up.
explanation.walkthrough: EER is the poetic e'er, ever.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim ruler or commander in Arabia.

clue.text: See 1
Aerospace technology to change with intervention of several years?

indicators.note: an intervention comes between, so one word is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: to alter is to change
a time is a period, such as several years

explanation.surface: A question of whether aviation technology will only change once years have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with intervention of' signals the insertion; the question mark admits 'several years' is a loose stand-in for time.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is the instrument aircraft use to measure their height above ground or sea level.

clue.text: A top teacher coming from Eton's changed: "I'm English and progressive"

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
of can mean coming from, as in a man of Kent

indicators.note: changed letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A headteacher who left Eton announces that they are a forward-looking Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' applies only to Eton's; the quoted speaker's I'm and English stay in place. 'coming from' is an old sense of of, as in a man of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ahead of their era has advanced ideas that later generations accept, which is what progressive describes.

clue.text: Waugh, say, bringing name forward, maintaining consistency

indicators.note: bringing a letter somewhere moves it, here within the name of the writer
forward means toward the front, so the moved letter ends up earlier in the word

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh was an English novelist, so Evelyn is an example of a Waugh

explanation.surface: A literary note that Evelyn Waugh's style stayed steady as he pushed his name to the fore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' and 'forward' move N in EVELYN to sit after EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something evenly means in a uniform, steady way, so the adverb means without variation.

clue.text: Work on sales pitch, overlooking one truthful message?

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: a spiel is a glib persuasive patter such as a sales pitch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice to polish a sales pitch while ignoring whether the message is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' drops I from SPIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gospel truth is something wholly reliable, so a gospel is a message taken as unquestionably true.

clue.text: Graduate turned up before exam, perfectly happy to cheat?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A postgraduate arrives before an exam with no qualms about cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes MA into AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any moral sense would have no scruples about dishonesty, so feels no guilt over deceiving.

clue.text: No idea why, but I'm at the scene

definitions.meaning: what you say when you cannot answer a question
read literally, the phrase means you have brought me to that place

explanation.surface: Someone baffled about why they have arrived somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why, but' only joins the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom admits ignorance, conceding a question is unanswerable, which is saying no idea.

clue.text: Energetic oil well sees abandonment of good conduct

indicators.note: abandoning a letter means dropping it from the word

parts.note: a gusher is an oil well that spouts forcefully

explanation.surface: A lively oil well where standards of behaviour have slipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conduct' looks like a noun meaning behaviour; it is the verb, to lead someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to show or lead them somewhere, the verbal sense of conduct.

clue.text: Two girls returning, with friend about, describing many of the sights of Egypt

definitions.text: describing many of the sights of Egypt

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the friend's letters go around the others

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Di and Mary are two girls' names

explanation.surface: Two girls come home with a friend after touring the ancient wonders of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns DIMARY into YRAMID.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyramidal means shaped like a pyramid, the form of Egypt's most famous ancient monuments.

clue.text: French engineer, in some reports, is quite a sight

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the word is taken by its spoken sound, and only some speakers make it match

parts.note: Gustave Eiffel was the French engineer behind the Eiffel Tower

explanation.surface: Accounts of a French engineer who cuts an impressive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some reports' admits the match only holds in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is informal for something or someone striking to look at, a remarkable spectacle.

clue.text: Security device: ranch will install one in actuality

indicators.note: installing something puts it inside, so these letters go within the ranch

parts.note: a ranch is a farm
I is the Roman numeral for one
in actuality is in reality, so real stands for actuality

explanation.surface: A ranch is actually going to have a security system fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will install' signals the insertion; 'in actuality' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a safety device that warns occupants when it detects smoke or flames.

clue.text: The French aristocrat not sentenced to the guillotine?

parts.note: le is French for the
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A French nobleman during the Revolution who escaped execution.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone let off has escaped punishment, here imagined as being spared the guillotine.

clue.text: Bore is quietly intense, not loud

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is removed

parts.note: fierce means intense, as in fierce heat
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A description of a tedious person who is intense but softly spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person; it is the verb to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to make one through something, which is to pierce it.

clue.text: Old lady supporting one in English mystery

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so this piece comes after
in places the numeral inside the abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
old lady is informal for mother, so ma

explanation.surface: An English whodunit with a mother propping up someone involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' means one's mother here, not an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or something baffling, a synonym of mystery.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise on getting a vision during eclipse

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in surprise when they witness a solar eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is British slang for wow.
explanation.definitionFit: The corona is the Sun's halo of outer atmosphere, seen only during a total solar eclipse.

clue.text: Abnormal reaction, sacking a Liberal following Conservative ministers

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed after the abbreviation
sacking means dismissing, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an allergy is an abnormal immune reaction

explanation.surface: Political news: a Tory government reacts badly and fires a Liberal minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' looks political; it means church ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy are the body of ordained ministers of a church collectively.

clue.text: Examinations reveal further cut on underside of hand

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the underside of means beneath, so this piece comes after

parts.note: fin is old slang for a hand

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: also means further, in addition

explanation.surface: Medical tests show a further cut on the palm of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims ALSO to ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Finals are the last examinations of a university degree course.

clue.text: Small island near France — the very thing for someone demanding solitude

parts.note: Herm is a small Channel Island near the French coast
it means the very thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A travel recommendation: a tiny island off France suits anyone after peace and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is one of the Channel Islands, British Crown dependencies off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is a recluse who lives apart from society by choice.

clue.text: Repeating requirement: "Time to oust MP"

indicators.note: ousting removes one occupant to put another in its place

parts.note: an imperative is an essential requirement

explanation.surface: A political slogan: an urgent demand that it is time the MP was thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust' puts T in place of MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterative describes a process of doing something over and over, which is to repeat.

clue.text: Size Small, arriving later in sudden rush

indicators.note: arriving later means the letter turns up further along in the word

parts.note: a spate is a sudden flood or rush

explanation.surface: Small-size clothes turn up late after a sudden surge in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Size' looks like a measurement; it is a glue used on paper and plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a gluey wash used to seal surfaces, a kind of paste.

clue.text: Sound of sheep initially dismissed after pastor finds fold

indicators.note: after means following, so the other piece comes second
dismissed initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bleat is the cry of a sheep

explanation.surface: A pastor tends his flock and hears the sheep go quiet in the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fold' looks like a sheep pen beside the pastor's flock; it is a crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed or stitched into fabric.

clue.text: Energy in giant mammals perverted sexual attraction

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of huge beasts whose vigour turns into a twisted lust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges E, IN, GIANT and MAMMALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal magnetism is a raw physical charisma that draws others, especially sexually.

clue.text: Identical trees moved into filming area for TV programme

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so these go within the filming area

parts.note: a set is the area where filming takes place
identical means the same

indicators.note: moved letters are shifted into a different order

explanation.surface: A film crew drags a row of matching trees on to the set for a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' signals an anagram of trees and 'into' puts it, after the synonym for identical, inside the filming area.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame Street is a long-running American children's television series featuring the Muppets.

clue.text: See 24
